ar_rollout_core.description: Closed-loop autoregressive generation of 7 chunks (21 frames, 3 frames/chunk, 4 denoising steps, Self-Forcing-like 5 s setting) at the paper's 90% target sparsity; tile budget = dense first chunk + 10% of every later chunk. Gym-generated values from the hidden test of the scaled closed-loop benchmark (reference runs of this iteration); not paper-reported numbers. The paper's own numbers are in the paper_* experiments.

mean_generation_rel_error.description: Relative L2 distance between the video generated with the method's sparse attention and the video generated with dense attention from the same noise, averaged over chunks and instances (closed loop: errors propagate through the KV cache). Bounded in [0, 2].

final_chunk_rel_error.description: Same distance on the last generated chunk only: accumulated autoregressive error at the end of the video.

revisit_rel_error.description: Same distance restricted to tokens that show a place filmed earlier but not within the last 6 frames before the chunk: long-range consistency / history forgetting.

mean_attention_cosine.description: Cosine similarity between the sparse and the dense attention output of every attention call, given identical inputs, averaged over calls and instances.

tile_cost_fraction.description: Attended tiles (+0.5 per probed tile) over the dense tile count. Context only: the evaluator enforces the experiment's tile budget as a hard constraint (exceeding it fails the run).

ar_rollout_long_context.description: Same at 10 chunks (30 frames): longer KV history, more cut-backs to places filmed long ago (LongLive-like longer generation). Gym-generated values from the hidden test of the scaled closed-loop benchmark (reference runs of this iteration); not paper-reported numbers. The paper's own numbers are in the paper_* experiments.

_notes.scaled_benchmark: The runnable experiments (ar_rollout_*) replace the paper's 1.3B video models and VBench with a closed-loop toy AR video-diffusion attention world; see scoring/EXPERIMENTS.md and HARDENING.md. Their results are the gym's own reference runs, not paper numbers.
